PHYSICAL CHESS • HOW TO PLAY

Controls, Calling Lets, Off-Back-Wall Drives & Pose Cam

1. Do I Have to Move My Player?

No — and that's the point. Squash's appeal is shot selection & timing, not keyboard gymnastics. The default is Shot-Select Mode (toggle with G or the top-left pill):

  • SHOT-SELECT MODE (Default — everyone starts here): You never run. Your Mii automatically moves to intercept the ball (including stepping into the back pocket to let deep drives come off the back glass wall) and recovers to the T-Position after each shot. Your entire job is choosing the shot and its timing.
  • MANUAL FOOTWORK (Advanced): Turn it off to control every step yourself with WASD or Arrow Keys (or Webcam Body Lunges) — adding footwork on top of shot selection is a steep curve, so come here once the shots feel natural.
  • AI vs AI Spectator Nudges: While watching AI vs AI, pressing 1–5 or WASD/Arrows nudges the next shot or footwork step without turning off autonomous AI play!

2. How Do I Swing & Shape Shots?

  • Hold & Release (Spacebar or Left-Click):
    • Hold down as the ball approaches to coil your backswing preparation.
    • Release normally → Tight Straight / Cross-Court Drive.
    • Hold Shift (or Right-Click) on release → Opens the racket face (+34° cut) for a Disguised Soft Drop into the front nick!
  • Direct Shot Hotkeys (Instant Swing): 1 Drive · 2 Cut Drop · 3 or B 2-Wall Boast (Shift+B Back-Wall Boast) · 4 High Lob · 5 Volley Kill · F or L Call Let · K Complete Rules · Esc/Q Menu.

3. Calling Lets, Strokes & On-Court Safety

In real squash, players share the same physical space and must never strike the ball when it risks hitting the opponent:

  • How to Call a Let Immediately: Press F or L, click ✋ Let (F), Raise an Open Palm ✋ in front of the Webcam, or Hold your Phone Vertically Upright (or tap Call Let on the phone pad).
  • Don't Hit Your Opponent! If you swing and hit your opponent with the ball, the Referee stops play, awards the Stroke/Let under WSF Rule 9, and issues a Formal Safety Warning to build safe real-life habits.
  • Call It or Lose It: If you are clearly obstructed and hold back your swing without calling a Let before the ball bounces twice, you lose the point ("Not Up!") and receive a Referee reminder!

4. Webcam Pose & Phone Inertial Racket

Click 📷 Pose Cam or 📱 Pocket Racket to play with motion sensors:

  • Webcam Swing & Let Signal: Whip your hand/forearm to strike; hold an Open Hand ✋ raised high for ~0.25s to appeal `"Let, please!"`.
  • Phone Inertial / Spatial Racket: Swing your phone to hit Drives/Drops/Boasts; hold the phone vertically upright (Pitch ≥ 58°) or tap the gold ✋ CALL LET! button to stop play safely.
WORLD SQUASH FEDERATION (WSF) • OFFICIAL SINGLES REFERENCE

📜 Complete Rules of the Game of Squash (Play Paused)

Official Rules & Public Reference URLs: 🌐 World Squash (WSF) Official Rules Portal ↗ 📄 WSF Singles Rules PDF (Full Text) ↗ 📘 US Squash Official Rules Guide ↗

1. The Court & Boundary Lines (Rule 1)

  • Dimensions: 9.75m long × 6.40m wide. Front Wall Out Line at 4.57m high; Back Wall Out Line at 2.13m high; sloped Side Wall Out Lines connecting them.
  • The Tin (0.48m Club / 0.43m PSA Pro): Runs across the bottom of the Front Wall. Any ball hitting the Tin or floor after the Front Wall is failed is "Down!".
  • Floor Markings: The Short Line (4.26m from Back Wall) and Half-Court Line form the "T" intersection. Two Service Boxes (1.60m × 1.60m) sit behind the Short Line.
  • Line Balls are OUT: A ball touching any Out Line, the Service Line (on serve), or the Tin bevel is Fault/Out.

2. Scoring Systems & Match Format (Rule 2)

  • PAR-11 (Point-A-Rally to 11 — Official WSF Standard): A point is scored by the winner of every rally, whether serving or receiving. Games are played to 11 points (must win by 2 clear points, e.g., 12–10). Matches are Best of 3 or Best of 5 games.
  • Hi-Ho 9 (Hand-In / Hand-Out to 9 — Traditional): Only the Server can score a point. When the Receiver wins a rally, they win the right to serve ("Handout") without the score changing. At 8–8, the Receiver chooses to play to 9 (Set 1) or 10 (Set 2).

3. The Serve & Service Faults (Rule 4)

  • Server's Position: At least one foot must be fully inside the Service Box (not touching any line) at the moment the racket strikes the ball (otherwise "Foot Fault!").
  • Legal Serve Trajectory: The ball must be dropped/tossed from the hand or racket and struck directly onto the Front Wall above the Service Line (1.78m) and below the Out Line (4.57m) so that—unless volleyed by the Receiver—its first floor bounce lands inside the opposite rear quarter-court behind the Short Line without hitting the Back Wall out line.
  • Alternating Boxes: When the Server wins a point, they switch to the other Service Box for the next serve. Upon winning a Handout, the new Server may choose either box.

4. A Good Return & Rally Play (Rules 5–7)

  • Before Second Bounce: To make a good return, the ball must be struck before it bounces twice on the floor (otherwise "Not Up!").
  • Reaching the Front Wall: A struck ball must reach the Front Wall above the Tin and below the Out Line. It may hit the Side Walls and/or Back Wall before or after hitting the Front Wall (e.g., 2-Wall Boast, 3-Wall Boast, Back-Wall Boast), provided it does not touch the floor or any Out Line first.

5. Interference: Calling Lets & Strokes (Rule 8)

Because both players share the same court, the player who just struck the ball must immediately make every effort to clear so the opponent has:

  1. A fair view of the ball on its rebound from the front wall;
  2. Unobstructed direct access to the ball;
  3. Freedom to strike the ball with a reasonable backswing and follow-through;
  4. Freedom to play the ball directly to any part of the front wall.
  • How to Request a Let: The obstructed player must stop play immediately and say "Let, please!" (Press F or L, click ✋ Let, raise an Open Palm ✋ on Webcam, or Hold Phone Upright). If you fail to call a clear Let and let the ball bounce twice, you lose the point!
  • No Let (Point to Non-Striker): Interference was minimal, the striker could not have reached the ball to make a good return, or the striker played past the interference and accepted it.
  • Yes, Let (Replay Rally): There was interference that the opponent made every effort to avoid, and the striker could have made a good return; OR the striker reasonably held back out of fear of hitting the opponent.
  • Stroke Awarded (Point to Striker): The opponent failed to make every effort to clear, stood inside the striker's reasonable swing arc, or stood directly in the front-wall shot triangle when the striker was poised to make a winning return.

6. Ball Hitting a Player & Safety Discipline (Rule 9)

  • Mandatory Safety Rule: A player must NEVER strike the ball if there is any risk of hitting the opponent with the ball or racket. Always stop play and appeal for a Let/Stroke!
  • Ball Hits Non-Striker Going Directly to Front Wall: It is a Stroke to the Striker—unless the striker had "turned" (let the ball pass behind their body and swung around the other side) or made a further attempt, in which case it is a Stroke to the Non-Striker.
  • Ball Hits Non-Striker via Another Wall (Boast): If the ball hits a side or back wall first before hitting the non-striker on its way to the front wall, it is a Yes, Let (unless it would have been a winning return, in which case a Stroke may be awarded).
  • Referee Safety Warning (Conduct Rule 15): Even when a player wins a Stroke because their ball hit an obstructing opponent, the Referee issues a Formal Safety Warning reminding the striker to stop and call a Let instead of hitting the opponent. Deliberate or dangerous play can result in a Conduct Stroke or Conduct Game!
